settings.title: Choker
settings.text: Sits close at the base of the neck. It's a very fitted length, so measure before you buy.

settings.title: Collarbone
settings.text: Rests on or just above the collarbone. Delicate on its own and the natural first layer in a stack.

settings.title: Upper chest
settings.text: Lands just below the collarbone. It works with crew necks, V-necks and open collars alike.

settings.title: Mid chest
settings.text: Drops a little further so a pendant has room to show. A good pick for high necklines.

settings.title: Long
settings.text: Falls towards the sternum. Relaxed and easy, and the length that holds a layered stack together.

settings.title: Close fit
settings.text: Sits neatly against smaller wrists with very little movement.

settings.title: Everyday fit
settings.text: Fits most wrists and moves a little without sliding over your hand. A reliable gifting size.

settings.title: Relaxed fit
settings.text: For larger wrists, chunkier chains or a loose, easy drape.

settings.question: Which necklace length is the most popular?
settings.answer: 18". It sits just below the collarbone and works with most necklines and neck sizes.

settings.question: Should I choose 16" or 18"?
settings.answer: Go for 16" if you want it close to the collarbone, or 18" for a little more drop. If you're torn, an adjustable 16"–18" style lets you wear both.

settings.question: What lengths work best for layering?
settings.answer: Leave roughly 2" between chains, for example 16", 18" and 20", so each one sits on its own line.

settings.question: Do thicker chains fit differently?
settings.answer: Yes. A heavier chain sits higher than a fine one of the same length, so consider going one size up.

settings.question: What length should I give as a gift?
settings.answer: 18" is the safest choice. Add an extender if you want extra flexibility.

settings.question: What is a typical bracelet size?
settings.answer: Most adult bracelets are between 6.5" and 8". Wrists vary a lot, so a quick measurement beats guessing.

settings.question: How can I measure without a tape measure?
settings.answer: Wrap string or a strip of paper around your wrist, mark where it meets, then measure it flat against a ruler.

settings.question: How tight should a bracelet be?
settings.answer: Not skin-tight. Most people add ¼" to 1" to their wrist measurement, depending on how loose they like it.

settings.question: Is bracelet size the same as watch size?
settings.answer: They're measured the same way, but watches are usually worn tighter because they don't drape.

settings.question: Should I size up for a chunky bracelet?
settings.answer: Usually yes, by about ½". Thicker pieces take up more room around the wrist.

settings.question: Can my wrist size change?
settings.answer: A little. Temperature, time of day and weight changes can all affect it, so re-measure now and then.

settings.title: Up to 10 mm
settings.text: A tiny initial, charm or single stone. It sits right in the dip of the collarbone on a 16"–18" chain.

settings.title: 12–18 mm
settings.text: Easy to see without being heavy. On an 18" chain it rests just below the collarbone.

settings.title: 20 mm +
settings.text: Coins, lockets and large shapes. Give them a longer 20"–22" chain so they hang freely instead of sitting on the collarbone.

settings.question: What if I'm between two sizes?
settings.answer: Choose the larger size, especially for wide bands. A ring that is slightly loose is more comfortable than one that pinches.

settings.question: Can I measure with a ring I already own?
settings.answer: Yes. Measure straight across the inside of the ring in millimetres and find that number in the Diameter column.

settings.question: Should a ring be tight or loose?
settings.answer: It should slide over your knuckle with a little effort and then feel secure, without spinning on your finger.

settings.question: Is my ring size the same on every finger?
settings.answer: No. Each finger is a slightly different size, so measure the finger you plan to wear the ring on.

settings.question: Can I order a ring as a gift without knowing the size?
settings.answer: Borrow a ring they wear on the same finger and measure its inside diameter. If that isn't possible, US 6–7 is the most common women's size.

settings.title: Sits on the lobe
settings.text: Sits flat on the lobe with no drop. Easy for every day and every piercing.

settings.title: 8–12 mm hoop
settings.text: A small hoop that wraps closely around the lobe. Great on its own or stacked.

settings.title: 2–3 cm
settings.text: Hangs just below the lobe and moves as you do. A simple way to dress up an outfit.

settings.title: 4 cm +
settings.text: Falls towards the jawline for more impact. Best in lighter pieces for all-day comfort.

settings.question: Which hoop size is the most popular?
settings.answer: 12–15 mm. They're small enough for every day but still visible.

settings.question: How is an earring drop measured?
settings.answer: From the piercing to the lowest point of the earring. For hoops, we give the outer diameter.

settings.question: Which earrings work for a second piercing?
settings.answer: Studs and huggies up to about 8 mm sit neatly without crowding the first piercing.

settings.question: Are long earrings heavy to wear?
settings.answer: Not if they're lightweight. Our longer drops are designed to be light enough to wear all day.
